$comment: Domain error codes are API surface. A client branches on the problem response's `type` URI, which is derived from the code, so renaming one breaks clients exactly as renaming a JSON field would - and just as invisibly. tools/check-error-codes.sh diffs this file against the codes actually raised, so a rename has to be a deliberate, reviewed change.

codes.meaning: A version was registered or added with a blank system prompt and no tools, so it could not do anything once activated.
The named version does not exist on this agent.

The caller is authenticated but policy refused the activation. The decision comes from OPA, and a sidecar that cannot be reached denies rather than allows, so this is also what an outage looks like to a client.
An agent name is already registered. Names are how humans and dashboards find an agent, so two agents cannot share one.
No agent with that identifier exists. Built by NotFoundException.of("Agent", id), so the code follows the type name rather than being written at the throw site.
The order was already cancelled. Refused rather than ignored, so a caller can tell a duplicate request from the first one.
Lines on one order were priced in different currencies. Refused rather than converted: an implicit conversion at an unstated rate is a financial defect.
An order was submitted with no lines. An empty order is refused, not stored as a draft.
No order with that identifier exists. Built by NotFoundException.of("Order", id), so the code follows the type name rather than being written at the throw site.
The request was malformed. The problem response carries an `errors` array of field/problem pairs. Retrying unchanged will fail the same way.
